summary: All 8 target claims had a substantive counter-evidence attempt and every target claim traces to a named sources.json entry, so no bounce was warranted in either direction. Original side: 7 of 8 claims hold, most with qualifications; the one clear downgrade is C5 (tool-fragmentation fatigue), which is vendor-asserted but unmeasured on both sides and cannot be called 'documented'. Two original framings were also cut back: faith.tools' 'most directly actionable' superlative (true on cost, unsupported on yield) and SmartGroups as a benchmark to 'match' (15 iOS ratings, no evidence of traction); vendor customer-base figures were reclassified from identification mechanic to market context since no customer list exists. Counter side: 2 claims hold cleanly (C1 job-board feed misses most churches by count, via independent FCT/Lifeway data; C2 faith.tools has a small audience), 4 hold partially (C3 traction finding survives but its freemium-conversion argument conflates objection removal with revenue conversion; C4 turnover risk survives but the intrinsic-motivation argument cuts the other way; C5 methodological point survives but Barna figures measure something other than fatigue; C6 minority framing is plausible but measures general tech sentiment, not in-meeting phone posture), 1 is an honest reported absence that actually strengthened the original (C7: Lifeway Research 2025 corroborates the Sept/Jan cadence), and 1 fails (C8: units mismatch and a market-size non-sequitur). Cross-cutting: the counter side's C1 implied conclusion is overstated because its own FCT source places 86% of worshippers in the churches the job-board feed samples, and the small-church target is an unverified plan assumption; the counter side reuses one vendor-sponsored Barna/Pushpay source for two claims. Seven questions remain genuinely unresolved, chiefly segment fit of the job-board feed, faith.tools yield, champion durability under volunteer turnover, and population-level prevalence of both app fatigue and in-meeting screen aversion.
